major_features: Confrontation detector for overlapping schedule configurations
Human-readable natural language translation of cron syntax
candidate_ideas.name: Cron Horizon
candidate_ideas.pain: Setting up a cron expression and accidentally triggering a heavy script every minute instead of every hour, or having two resource-intensive jobs run simultaneously and crash the server.
candidate_ideas.problem: Cron expressions are hard to read, debug, and predict, leading to unexpected job execution times or resource-heavy overlaps.
candidate_ideas.solution: A local-first cron visualizer that parses standard cron syntax, generates an interactive 12-month calendar projection, and flags potential concurrency conflicts.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Developers, DevOps engineers, and system administrators.
candidate_ideas.verification: Paste a specific cron expression (e.g., '*/15 9-17 * * 1-5'), verify that the generated run-times list matches expected 15-minute intervals during business hours on weekdays.

major_features: Tap-to-sync time stamping with spacebar keypresses
Real-time visual wave preview of loaded local media
Instant export to standard SRT and WebVTT formats
candidate_ideas.name: SubSync Studio
candidate_ideas.pain: Free tools are filled with ads or upload data to remote servers, while manual timestamp editing in a text editor is slow and error-prone.
candidate_ideas.problem: Generating SRT/WebVTT subtitles for short videos without expensive cloud services or uploading sensitive files is tedious.
candidate_ideas.solution: A client-side HTML5 app where you load a local media file and a plain-text transcript, then 'tap-to-sync' by pressing spacebar as the audio plays to record exact timestamps, exporting a clean SRT file.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Content creators, educators, and accessibility specialists.
candidate_ideas.verification: Load a sample audio file and text paragraph, tap spacebar at intervals, and verify the exported SRT file contains correct progressive timestamps.

major_features: Interactive dependency tree mapping files and assets
Broken link and orphaned image asset diagnostic report
candidate_ideas.name: DocuLink Validator
candidate_ideas.pain: Broken links in static-site documentation are often only caught after production deployment or by frustrated users filing issues.
candidate_ideas.problem: Reorganizing markdown documentation folders breaks relative file paths and image references.
candidate_ideas.solution: A browser-based folder auditor that parses dropped markdown folders, maps all relative links, and outputs an interactive error log of broken references and orphaned images.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Technical writers, product managers, and developers.
candidate_ideas.verification: Drag and drop a mock folder structure containing markdown files with broken relative paths and verify the application highlights the exact files and line numbers with broken links.

major_features: Interactive visual grid builder with click-and-drag cell merging
Nested CSS Flexbox alignment and spacing controller
Real-time responsive viewport simulation with clean code exporter
candidate_ideas.name: FlexGrid Scaffolder
candidate_ideas.pain: Writing CSS layout code by hand often leads to layout shifts, redundant wrapper divs, and bloated CSS files.
candidate_ideas.problem: Translating a visual layout design into clean, responsive CSS Grid and Flexbox code requires tedious manual coordinate calculations.
candidate_ideas.solution: A visual canvas where users drag and resize layout cells, nest flex containers, and instantly copy clean, semantic HTML and CSS with zero external dependencies.
candidate_ideas.verification: Create a 3x3 grid, merge two cells, adjust fractional widths, and verify that the exported CSS contains valid grid-template-columns and grid-area definitions.

major_features: Local, deterministic mock data generation with zero external APIs
Bulk export options for JSON, CSV, and SQL insert formats
candidate_ideas.name: SchemaMock Artisan
candidate_ideas.pain: Using public web APIs to generate mock data can expose proprietary database schemas or sensitive data structures to third parties.
candidate_ideas.problem: Developers need realistic mock JSON datasets adhering to specific schemas for testing, but writing custom generator scripts takes too much time.
candidate_ideas.solution: A local-first JSON generator where users visually construct schema models (e.g., nested objects, arrays, specific data types like names, emails, UUIDs) and instantly export thousands of valid mock records.
candidate_ideas.verification: Define a schema with user profiles containing names and emails, generate 100 records, and verify the output is valid JSON matching the exact schema constraints.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; it does not claim live market research.
Generated projects are constrained to dependency-free local browser apps for safe deterministic validation.
